stack_spec.name: Built with Spec4 (BWS4)
stack_spec.description: A unified web app that showcases Spec4 through a gallery of illustrative example apps demonstrating agentic AI patterns: retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), tool-use, a visual embeddings explorer, a single-call (simple vs. structured-output) demo, and a two-step chained-calls (role-played writer/critic) demo.

languages.name: Python
languages.role: backend service — REST API, LiteLLM/OpenRouter orchestration, RAG pipeline, embeddings example app (embedding + PCA projection), single-call example app (simple/structured generation), chained-calls example app (two-step role-played generation via PydanticAI), shared framework services, Neon/Postgres access

languages.name: TypeScript
languages.role: browser client — single-page app presenting the landing page and all example apps

targets.name: web_client
targets.purpose: the browser UI presenting the landing page and every example app (RAG, tool-use, embeddings, single-call, chained-calls, future patterns), with per-example-app code-splitting so the gallery can grow without bloating the initial load
targets.hosting: Render Static Site (free tier — no spin-down, served via CDN)
targets.build: Vite build producing a hashed static bundle with route-based lazy-loaded chunks per example app
targets.distribution: served at the app's root domain

targets.name: api
targets.purpose: serves the SPA's data needs — LiteLLM/OpenRouter orchestration, RAG pipeline (chunking, embedding, retrieval), embeddings example app (preconfigured/custom text embedding and 2D projection), single-call example app (simple text and structured/schema-conforming generation), chained-calls example app (two-step role-played generation via PydanticAI/OpenRouter), Exa search integration, and shared framework services (generation, embedding, storage)
targets.runtime: Python 3.12 on a Render free Web Service (spins down after ~15 min idle; cold-starts on next request; 750 free instance-hours/month)
targets.build: container image or native Python buildpack from the repo
targets.api_contract: REST; OpenAPI schema auto-generated by FastAPI

exposure.cors: allow only the web_client's own origin

capabilities.capability_class: a capable general-purpose free model for grounded, structured-output answers (meta-llama/llama-3.3-70b-instruct:free)
a fast alternate free model, also strong at structured/tool-oriented output (google/gemini-2.0-flash-exp:free)
a capable general-purpose free model able to produce both plain text and JSON-schema-conforming structured output for a single direct prompt/response demo (meta-llama/llama-3.3-70b-instruct:free)
a fast alternate free model, also strong at structured/JSON output, for the single-call demo

OpenRouter (via LiteLLM).fallback: Gemini 2.0 Flash free takes over automatically via LiteLLM routing if the primary Llama 3.3 70B free model's rate limit is hit or it errors, for both the RAG and single-call tiers

capabilities.capability_class: a capable general-purpose free model able to sustain a distinct role-played persona (struggling writer, harsh critic) across a two-step sequential chain (meta-llama/llama-3.3-70b-instruct:free)
a fast alternate free model, also strong at persona/role-played and structured JSON output, for the chained-calls demo

OpenRouter (via PydanticAI).fallback: Gemini 2.0 Flash free takes over automatically via PydanticAI's native FallbackModel if the primary Llama 3.3 70B free model errors or hits its rate limit, for either step of the chain; both models' slugs are read from the same shared model-slug config module used by the LiteLLM lane

integrations.name: Exa Search API
integrations.purpose: fetch ranked, real external search results (title, summary, source) so tool-use example apps can incorporate outside information

primary_store.purpose: durable relational store for everything the app writes, doubling as the vector index for the RAG example app
primary_store.durability: source of truth; survives restarts and redeploys; Neon's free tier persists indefinitely (unlike Render's free Postgres, which expires after 30 days)

embedding_projection_cache.choice: in-process NumPy array of preconfigured embeddings + fitted PCA model, held in memory (all-MiniLM-L6-v2 vectors, scikit-learn PCA)
embedding_projection_cache.purpose: fills the vector_index substrate for the embeddings example app's custom_text_semantic_placement capability: holds the preconfigured examples' embeddings and the fitted PCA projection so a new custom-text point can be transformed into the same stable 2D layout without recomputing it, and without persisting user-entered custom text beyond the request per the capability's privacy requirement
embedding_projection_cache.durability: ephemeral — rebuilt from bundled_assets' preconfigured_text_examples at process startup or on first request; ephemeral in-process derived state, rebuildable, not a source of truth; custom text embeddings exist only for the duration of the request and are never persisted

collections.name: preconfigured_example_embeddings
physical: in-process NumPy array, 384-dim (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) per preconfigured example
fitted PCA model held in memory, reused via .transform() for custom text

bundled_assets.choice: static content bundled at build time
bundled_assets.purpose: read-only content that only changes via a code change/redeploy, not user action

collections.name: preconfigured_text_examples
collections.purpose: the curated set of words, short phrases, and sentences spanning multiple categories used to seed the embeddings example app's plot

collections.name: preset_prompts
collections.purpose: the curated set of example prompts (e.g. summarize, classify, extract) with their labeled intent, offered as one-click choices in the single-call example app

collections.name: persona_prompt_templates
collections.purpose: static system-prompt templates and few-shot exemplars defining the 'struggling writer' and 'harsh critic' personas used by the two chained calls; read-only, versioned in-repo alongside the RAG and single-call prompt conventions

browser_local_storage.purpose: keeps the visitor's light/dark theme choice across visits without a backend round trip
browser_local_storage.durability: persists per-device/browser only; not a source of truth, not shared across devices

chunking_pipeline.choice: hand-rolled paragraph/fixed-window text splitter, in application code
chunking_pipeline.purpose: splits reference_dataset documents into passages before embedding; kept simple and transparent given the small curated dataset, serving the project's teaching-clarity goal

embedding_pipeline.choice: sentence-transformers (all-MiniLM-L6-v2), in-process at index time and query time
embedding_pipeline.purpose: fills the catalog's embedding_pipeline substrate for both the RAG example (vectors written to and read from dataset_embeddings) and the embeddings example app (vectors for preconfigured examples and custom text, held in embedding_projection_cache) — the same shared embedding model is reused rather than introduced separately

retriever.choice: SQLAlchemy query using pgvector's cosine-distance operator against dataset_embeddings
retriever.purpose: finds the top-N passages most similar to a question's embedding, to ground the generated answer

pipeline_runner.choice: PydanticAI, using its OpenRouterProvider and native FallbackModel to run the fixed two-step 'struggling writer' → 'harsh critic' sequence, with the first call's response passed directly as the second call's input
pipeline_runner.purpose: fills the catalog's pipeline_runner substrate for the chained-calls example app; chosen over a hand-rolled function because upcoming example apps will coordinate multiple agents, and PydanticAI's typed Agent/delegation primitives extend naturally to that without a framework swap; chosen over LangChain/LangGraph as lighter-weight and free of state-graph/checkpointing machinery this fixed 2-step demo doesn't need; the free-model slugs used by its OpenRouterProvider and FallbackModel are read from the same shared model-slug config module the LiteLLM lane uses, and the existing usage_limits/service_log_entries quota-check function gates calls on this path exactly as it gates the LiteLLM path

ai_conventions.prompt_versioning: the rag_example_app's prompt template (including its structured-output schema/instructions) is stored as a versioned file in-repo (e.g. backend/app/rag/prompts/answer_v1.md), tagged with a semantic version in the filename/header, and loaded by a thin resolver function; the single_call_example_app's preset prompts follow the same convention — plain text/intent metadata stored in-repo (e.g. backend/app/single_call/prompts/presets.py or a versioned data file), with any structured-mode JSON schemas defined alongside as versioned Pydantic models; the chained_calls_example_app's 'struggling writer' and 'harsh critic' persona system-prompt templates follow the identical convention — versioned files under backend/app/chained_calls/prompts/ (e.g. writer_v1.md, critic_v1.md), loaded by the same thin resolver pattern; no external prompt-management tool

libraries.name: FastAPI
libraries.purpose: REST API framework, async-native, generates OpenAPI schema from Pydantic models

libraries.name: SQLAlchemy
libraries.purpose: ORM/toolkit for Neon Postgres access, including pgvector column types

libraries.name: asyncpg
libraries.purpose: async PostgreSQL driver used by SQLAlchemy's async engine to connect to Neon

libraries.name: Alembic
libraries.purpose: versioned schema migrations for the Postgres/Neon schema

libraries.name: httpx
libraries.purpose: async HTTP client for calling the Exa Search API without blocking the event loop

libraries.name: Pydantic
libraries.purpose: request/response validation, structured-output schema for the RAG answer format, and per-preset schema models for the single-call example app's Structured mode (validating the LiteLLM JSON response and surfacing nonconformance as a ValidationError)

libraries.name: LiteLLM
libraries.purpose: unified interface to OpenRouter's free models for text generation, with built-in retry/fallback across the primary and fallback model, used by RAG and by the single-call example app's simple and structured-output requests

libraries.name: PydanticAI
libraries.purpose: agent framework running the chained-calls example app's fixed two-step 'struggling writer' → 'harsh critic' sequence via its OpenRouterProvider and native FallbackModel; chosen (over a hand-rolled function) because it extends cleanly to future example apps that coordinate multiple agents, and (over LangChain/LangGraph) as the lighter-weight option free of state-graph/checkpointing overhead this fixed-length demo doesn't need

libraries.name: sentence-transformers
libraries.purpose: in-process local embedding model (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) for text representation at index and query time, shared by the RAG pipeline and the embeddings example app so both use the same embedding representation

libraries.name: scikit-learn
libraries.purpose: PCA dimensionality reduction, fitted once on the preconfigured examples' embeddings and reused via .transform() for custom text, so the 2D layout stays stable across recalculations rather than jumping when a new point is added

libraries.name: pgvector
libraries.purpose: Python/SQLAlchemy client for the pgvector Postgres extension, enabling vector columns and similarity queries

libraries.name: pydantic-settings
libraries.purpose: typed, validated configuration objects reading env vars/.env files (API keys, DB URL, Sentry DSN)

libraries.name: structlog
libraries.purpose: structured JSON logging for application events and service-log entries

libraries.name: sentry-sdk
libraries.purpose: backend error tracking and aggregation across FastAPI, LiteLLM, PydanticAI, and Exa calls (free tier)

libraries.name: pytest
libraries.purpose: backend test runner

libraries.name: React
libraries.purpose: UI framework for the single-page app

libraries.name: Vite
libraries.purpose: frontend build tool and dev server, with native code-splitting support

libraries.name: React Router
libraries.purpose: client-side routing with lazy-loaded routes, one per example app

libraries.name: TanStack Query
libraries.purpose: data fetching, caching, and loading/error state management for calls to the API

libraries.name: Tailwind CSS
libraries.purpose: utility-first styling enforcing a consistent visual language and light/dark theming across all example apps, including the single-call example app's plain-text and formatted-JSON displays

libraries.name: plotly.js

libraries.name: react-plotly.js
libraries.purpose: React component wrapper around plotly.js used to render the embeddings scatter plot declaratively, ships its own TypeScript declarations

libraries.name: Vitest
libraries.purpose: frontend unit/component test runner, Vite-native

libraries.name: React Testing Library
libraries.purpose: component testing focused on user-visible behavior

libraries.name: Playwright
libraries.purpose: end-to-end browser testing of full user flows across the deployed SPA and API

libraries.name: @sentry/react
libraries.purpose: frontend error tracking for unhandled exceptions and failed requests, unified with the backend Sentry project (free tier)

project_structure.purpose: FastAPI routers, one module per feature (landing, RAG, tool-use, embeddings, single-call, chained-calls, shared services)

shared framework services: LLM access (LiteLLM wrapper), embedding (sentence-transformers wrapper), storage abstraction, shared model-slug config, and the usage-limit quota-check/logging function reused by both the LiteLLM and PydanticAI call paths
RAG-specific logic: chunking pipeline, retriever, versioned prompt templates
embeddings example app logic: bundled preconfigured TextExample set, in-process embedding + PCA fit/transform, and the API route accepting custom text and returning the recalculated 2D projection

single-call example app logic: bundled PresetPrompt set, per-preset Pydantic schema models for Structured mode, and the API route accepting a prompt/preset + mode selection and returning a plain-text or structured (request+response) result via the shared LiteLLM generation service

chained-calls example app logic: PydanticAI agent setup (OpenRouterProvider + FallbackModel using the shared model-slug config), the two-step writer→critic run function, and the API route accepting the initial request and returning the intermediate and final outputs
versioned persona system-prompt templates ('struggling writer', 'harsh critic') following the project's in-repo prompt-versioning convention
SQLAlchemy models, session factory, Alembic migrations
pytest suites mirroring the package layout
one folder per screen: landing, RAG example, tool-use example, embeddings example, single-call example, chained-calls example, framework console
one folder per example app (rag, tool-use, embeddings, single-call, chained-calls, and future additions), each lazy-loaded via its own route
the embeddings example app's route module: plot component (react-plotly.js), custom-text input, and the educational explanation of the embedding pattern

the single-call example app's route module: prompt input and preset selector, Simple/Structured mode toggle, plain-text response view, side-by-side structured request/response JSON view (rendered via JSON.stringify in a styled <pre> block), and the educational explanation of the single-call pattern

the chained-calls example app's route module: initial-request input, upfront description of each call's role, labeled intermediate-output and final-output blocks, the quota-conservation notice (capped at exactly 2 calls), and the educational explanation of the chained-calls pattern
shared UI: nav bar, theme toggle, layout shell
typed API client and TanStack Query hooks calling the backend
route configuration with lazy (React.lazy) imports per example app

patterns: functional core / imperative shell — pure functions for chunking/retrieval/scoring logic, PCA fit/transform, single-call schema validation, and the chained-calls writer→critic sequencing, thin FastAPI route handlers as the imperative shell
dependency injection for shared services (LiteLLM client, PydanticAI agents, DB session, Exa client) via FastAPI's Depends
React: function components and hooks only, no class components
custom hooks for shared frontend logic (e.g. useExampleApps, useTheme)
documentation: Google-style docstrings on every public Python function
JSDoc on every exported TypeScript function

references.standard: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks (Lewis et al.)
Prompt Engineering Guide (general single-call prompting reference)
Building Effective Agents (prompt chaining / workflow pattern overview, Anthropic)
